articleBlocks: The initial clues felt random. Brown could be a color, Rice a grain, and Duke a title.
I was missing a clear pattern.
My first thought was that they were all elite colleges, but that felt too broad. I needed a more specific connection.
The inclusion of Sorbonne and Oxford shifted my perspective. These are both famous European universities.
That's when it clicked: they are all names of universities.
The answer is names of universities. Each clue represents a distinct institution.
Brown is Brown University, Rice is Rice University, and Duke is Duke University.
Sorbonne points to Sorbonne University in Paris, and Oxford is Oxford University in England.
The initial misdirection made the final answer more satisfying.
Now the clues form a clear and recognizable category.
The full set confirms that each clue is a well-known university.

solutionNarrative: Brown and Rice first pulled me toward famous schools, so that was the first path I tested. It held together for a moment, but oxford never really fit it. The more I pushed that first read, the more the board sounded stitched together instead of naturally solved.

The solve turned when I stopped treating oxford as just another clue and asked what kind of thing each clue could really be describing. Once I made that shift, I was no longer thinking about famous schools; I was checking whether the earlier clues all behaved like parts of the same real set. That was when the answer became clear, because the remaining clues stopped feeling like separate trivia and started reinforcing the real category.
